cases.question: Starting from Spring's Kotlin PropertyResolver convenience APIs, trace typed, default-valued, required and bracket-operator property lookup into a PropertySourcesPropertyResolver and the Java helpers it uses. Discover the cross-language handoffs and explain the five requested mechanisms, including ordered sources, nested placeholders, conversion and failure boundaries. The receiver uses the stock implementation with an ordinary finite ordered PropertySources collection; a source or configured conversion service may return null or throw. No concurrent mutation is assumed. Stay at the lookup, placeholder-helper and conversion-service boundaries: do not enumerate converter implementations, the full placeholder grammar/escape configuration, containsProperty, validateRequiredProperties or environment construction. Do not execute the repository or treat Kotlin's declared non-null return type as a promise that every lookup succeeds. For each finding, cite one representative implementation mechanism in one contiguous range of at most 40 physical lines; explain other inspected branches in prose without stitching quotations.

findings.description: Explain the bracket operator and all three generic convenience forms, their return nullability and inline/reified non-null type bound, and the exact Java overload arguments they delegate. Distinguish Java runtime-Class passing from generic collection-element preservation and from implementing lookup/default/required policy in Kotlin. Cite the generic extension declarations and explain the operator in prose.
findings.marker: inline fun <reified T : Any> PropertyResolver.getProperty(key: String, default: T) : T =

findings.description: Follow ordinary, typed and raw-string lookup into the source loop. Explain iteration precedence, null values/no collection/no match, and exactly when the first raw non-null value ends source search. Include whether null conversion results or processing exceptions try a later source, and whether repeated lookups cache prior results or reread sources. Cite the lookup loop.

Explain which String and non-String CharSequence values receive nested resolution for which target types, ordering relative to conversion, and how raw lookup differs. Follow empty-value handling, default strict versus configured permissive nested behavior, direct strict/non-strict APIs, lazy helper separation and the raw-property callback used by the helper. Distinguish helper caching from value caching. Cite the nested-resolution/helper handoff and explain the source-loop conditions in prose.

Explain the null-target and already-assignable fast paths, use of the shared default service when conversion is necessary, and how an explicitly set service changes those branches. Also follow getConversionService's lazy independent service, its initialization guard and how calling it affects later lookups. Explain setter null validation, conversion null returns and exceptions without asserting every value is convertible. Cite convertValueIfNecessary and explain getter/setter initialization in prose.

Follow default-valued and required lookup into their Java implementations. Explain whether fallback/required handling happens before or after lookup, placeholder processing and conversion; distinguish missing/null results from exceptions; and identify the required-lookup exception type. Include a selected source whose conversion returns null and why these wrappers do not restart source selection. Cite the typed default and required branches.
